title: Enable rpathification and working relocation on Linux
description:
Dumpcap depends on wsutil.so. The path to the shared library
is encoded in the RPATH (or RUNPATH) property of ELF binaries.
This is currently an absolute path on most Unixy systems.

Dumpcap could not be made to work with a relative RPATH because it
uses elevated privileges and some loaders will ignore relative
RPATHs and non-standard paths under those circumstances, because of
(justified) security concerns.

To enable relocation of the program we link dumpcap statically
with wsutil instead.

This provides a fully working relocatable installation on Linux
and other platforms that support relative RPATHs.

notes.body:
For what it's worth, [the Linux ld.so man page](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/ld.so.8.html) says:

```
Dynamic string tokens
       In several places, the dynamic linker expands dynamic string
       tokens:

       o  In the environment variables LD_LIBRARY_PATH, LD_PRELOAD, and
          LD_AUDIT,

       o  inside the values of the dynamic section tags DT_NEEDED,
          DT_RPATH, DT_RUNPATH, DT_AUDIT, and DT_DEPAUDIT of ELF
          binaries,

       o  in the arguments to the ld.so command line options --audit,
          --library-path, and --preload (see below), and

       o  in the filename arguments to the dlopen(3) and dlmopen(3)
          functions.

       The substituted tokens are as follows:

       $ORIGIN (or equivalently ${ORIGIN})
              This expands to the directory containing the program or
              shared object.  Thus, an application located in
              somedir/app could be compiled with

                  gcc -Wl,-rpath,'$ORIGIN/../lib'

              so that it finds an associated shared object in
              somedir/lib no matter where somedir is located in the
              directory hierarchy.  This facilitates the creation of
              "turn-key" applications that do not need to be installed
              into special directories, but can instead be unpacked into
              any directory and still find their own shared objects.
```

[The FreeBSD 8.0 ld.so man page](https://www.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=ld.so&apropos=0&sektion=0&manpath=FreeBSD+8.0-RELEASE&arch=default&format=html) and later pages, [the NetBSD 5.0 ld_elf.so man page](https://man.netbsd.org/NetBSD-5.0/ld.elf_so.1) and later pages, [the current DragonFly BSD rtld man page](https://man.dragonflybsd.org/?command=rtld&section=ANY), and [the Solaris 7 ld.so.1 man page](https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E19620-01/805-3172/805-3172.pdf) all mention $ORIGIN.  (I suspect it originated at Sun and was picked up by other UN*Xes that use ELF as the executable format.)

At least in Solaris, `$ORIGIN` is required to point to a "trusted directory" in a "secure process", as per [the "Security in Coded Processes" section of the Solaris 11.4 Linkers and Libraries Guide](https://docs.oracle.com/en/operating-systems/solaris/oracle-solaris/11.4/linkers-libraries/security-coded-processes.html).  (Note that the example exploit is making a hard link, not a symbolic link, so expanding symbolic links when constructing `$ORIGIN` wouldn't close that hole.)  "secure process" includes set-UID and set-GID processes, and "trusted directory" may not include /usr/local.  The GNU libc ld.so seems to do something similar; the FreeBSD ld.so doesn't appear to have any notion of trusted directories and appears to just fail to expand `$ORIGIN` in set-UID/set-GID processes.

So not as useful as one might like.

This change obviates the need to use $ORIGIN with dumpcap, for the reasons you mention.

Because dumpcap is linked statically with wsutil, there is nothing to link to at runtime (other than system libraries in trusted locations), so $ORIGIN being ignored has no effect on the program. We could remove it from dumpcap's RPATH, but that isn't necessary. Other programs like Wireshark work fine with $ORIGIN. dumpcap was the limitation.

Unless I misunderstood your point.

The point was that `$ORIGIN` might provide a way to support set-UID/set-GID programs as part of a package that includes shared libraries, with the set-UID/set-GID programs using some of those shared libraries, and having the package be relocatable, but it's complicated and may only work if the package is in a "trusted directory", so it might not be the way we'd want to do it.
It does work. At least on Linux (with GNU ld.so).

Tests failed on MacOS.  

https://github.com/wireshark/wireshark/actions/runs/4039216599/jobs/6943744416  
  
```
2023-01-30T00:03:00.9987880Z Failed to detect tshark features: 
Command '('/Users/runner/work/wireshark/wireshark/build/run/tshark', '--version')' died with <Signals.SIGABRT: 6>.
```
I'm aware that this is causing problems on macOS but I don´t have any way to test it so unless someone else can fix it the commit should be reverted.
`build.ninja` on macOS shows that each of our executables links with both `run/libwsutil_static.a` and `run/libwsutil.0.0.0.dylib` with this change. Reversion inbound in !9647.

I think I found the issue, which is that `libui` has a CMake dependency on `wiretap` and non-static `wsutil`.

But feel free to revert it and I'll take it up again some other time.

Would be helpful to have a macOS build for MRs by the way. Is this unfeasible? I don´t remember if there has been any discussion about it.

I think the `libui` issue was part of the problem, but Wireshark, tshark, and other executables were linking with libwsutil_static.a as well.

GitLab announced a beta program for shared macOS runners a while back but access was limited. It looks like they opened it up somewhat so I opened a request to add wireshark/wireshark.

The issue is specific to priviliges.c (at least one issue, there's probably more) by having more than one symbol for `init_process_policies_called` with static linking. Some arcane linker behaviour I haven't been able to make out yet makes it work more-or-less OK on Linux but not macOS.

Nice, thanks.

changes_data.diff:
@@ -36,6 +36,9 @@ Previously it was ``$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/wireshark/extcap``.
 The installation target no longer installs development headers by default.
 That must be done explicitly using ``cmake --install <builddir> --component Development``.
 
+The Wireshark installation is relocatable on Linux (and other ELF platforms
+with support for relative RPATHs).
+
 Many other improvements have been made.
 See the “New and Updated Features” section below for more details.

@@ -269,26 +269,25 @@ if(NOT (WIN32 OR APPLE OR USE_STATIC))
 		# Some systems support $ORIGIN in RPATH to enable relocatable
 		# binaries. In other cases, only absolute paths can be used.
 		# https://www.lekensteyn.nl/rpath.html
+		#
+		# Also note that some systems (notably those using GNU libc)
+		# silently ignore $ORIGIN in RPATH for binaries that are
+		# setuid root or use privileged capabilities.
+		#
 		if(CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME MATCHES "^(Linux|SunOS|FreeBSD)$")
 			set(_enable_rpath_origin TRUE)
-			if(BUILD_dumpcap AND ENABLE_PCAP)
-				# dumpcap will most likely be installed with
-				# capabilities or setuid. Relative RPATHs that
-				# resolve to non-standard library directories
-				# are ignored for such binaries and since we
-				# cannot achieve relocatable builds, just
-				# disable it by default.
-				set(_enable_rpath_origin FALSE)
-			endif()
-			# Provide a knob to optionally force absolute rpaths,
-			# to support old/buggy systems and as a user preference
-			# for hardening.
-			set(ENABLE_RPATH_ORIGIN ${_enable_rpath_origin} CACHE BOOL
-				"Use $ORIGIN with INSTALL_RPATH")
-			mark_as_advanced(ENABLE_RPATH_ORIGIN)
 		else()
-			set(ENABLE_RPATH_ORIGIN FALSE)
+			set(_enable_rpath_origin FALSE)
 		endif()
+
+		# Provide a knob to optionally force absolute rpaths,
+		# to support old/buggy systems and as a user preference
+		# for hardening.
+		# XXX Should this be a CMake option?
+		set(ENABLE_RPATH_ORIGIN ${_enable_rpath_origin} CACHE BOOL
+			"Use $ORIGIN with INSTALL_RPATH")
+		mark_as_advanced(ENABLE_RPATH_ORIGIN)
+
 		if(ENABLE_RPATH_ORIGIN)
 			set(LIBRARY_INSTALL_RPATH     "$ORIGIN")
 			set(EXECUTABLE_INSTALL_RPATH  "$ORIGIN/../${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}")
@@ -3131,7 +3130,7 @@ endif()
 if(BUILD_dumpcap AND PCAP_FOUND)
 	set(dumpcap_LIBS
 		writecap
-		wsutil
+		wsutil_static
 		caputils
 		ui
 		version_info
